events.title: Google Agent Anomaly Detection: Out-of-Band Security Oversight for Autonomous Agents
events.tldr: Google launched Agent Anomaly Detection on Gemini Enterprise, performing asynchronous, reasoning-based security audits mapped directly to the OWASP Agentic Top 10.
events.what_happened: Google introduced an out-of-band security and auditing layer that analyzes OpenTelemetry traces, reasoning steps, and tool calls of production agents without slowing response time.
events.what_changed: Traditional unit tests or standard latency/token metrics fail to catch silent privilege escalations or improper tool calls. Google's tool inspects the complete execution graph asynchronously against OWASP Agentic Top 10 risks.
events.why_it_matters: Solves the core enterprise dilemma: autonomous agents make runtime decisions that bypass traditional static code security filters, requiring behavioral trace monitoring.
key_takeaways: Asynchronous out-of-band evaluation ensures zero impact on live latency.
Native mapping to OWASP Agentic Top 10 (ASI02 Tool Misuse, ASI03 Privilege Abuse, ASI10 Rogue Agents).
Integration with Security Command Center for centralized incident triage.
technical_architecture: OpenTelemetry trace collector ingesting agent tool calls and reasoning logs.
Asynchronous reasoning-based audit engine.
Security Command Center publisher.
technical_details: Flags subtle intent shifts and unexpected tool reach.
Provides plain-language risk explanations and actionable remediations.
Upcoming support for custom business logic rules written in natural language.
events.potential_impact: Sets the enterprise standard for non-blocking agent behavioral security monitoring.
events.action: Review OWASP Agentic Top 10 categories (ASI02, ASI03, ASI08, ASI10) and document potential failure modes in your agent projects.

events.title: Title-Partitioning Strategies: Frontier LLM Self-Communication Efficiency in Information Asymmetry Games
events.tldr: Evaluating frontier LLMs in a two-agent log(N)-Questions game reveals that models achieve optimal 1 bit/question efficiency specifically when partitioning context by document titles.
events.what_happened: A study evaluated 6 frontier LLMs in a paired information asymmetry game (log2(N) questions over Wikipedia abstracts) to measure model self-communication efficiency.
events.what_changed: Previous evaluations measured model single-prompt QA accuracy. This benchmark tests how efficiently a model can reduce search space entropy when split into an information-limited questioner and answerer.
events.why_it_matters: Teaches crucial prompt design principles for multi-agent systems: structured indexing (like binary splitting on document titles) dramatically outperforms unstructured reasoning.
key_takeaways: Win rate scales smoothly as p^(log2 N) with average per-round reliability p=0.928.
Only top models extracted a full 1 bit of information per question by using title-partitioning strategies.
Excessive reasoning-token expenditure showed little correlation with game success.
technical_architecture: Paired 2-agent information game protocol.
Strict log2(N) yes/no constraint.
Entropy reduction metric (bits per question).
technical_details: 408 games evaluated across document sets up to 1024 paragraphs.
Tested GLM-5.3, GPT-5.6 Sol, Grok 4.6, Gemini 3.8 Flash, Kimi K3, and Claude Opus 5.
Identified strict bias toward defaulting to 'No' answers in weaker models.
events.potential_impact: Informs structured protocol design for multi-agent negotiation, binary search tree retrieval, and active learning loops.
events.action: Analyze binary search partitioning logic in multi-agent prompt design to optimize information gathering loops.

events.title: LimiX-2: Contextual Mechanism Networks for Zero-Shot Tabular Causal Recovery
events.category: AI Research / Structured Data & Causal ML
events.tldr: LimiX-2 introduces Contextual Mechanism Networks (CMNs) pretrained on Structural Causal Models to achieve state-of-the-art zero-shot tabular prediction and causal skeleton recovery.
events.what_happened: Researchers released LimiX-2, a foundation model for structured data trained using Context-Conditional Masked Modeling (CCMM) over synthetic datasets from Structural Causal Models (SCMs).
events.what_changed: Traditional tabular models focus on target-centric prediction p(y|x, D_context). LimiX-2 models joint probability distributions p(x,y|D_context), capturing underlying data-generating mechanisms.
events.why_it_matters: Enables agents working with SQL databases and tabular analytics to infer causal relationships and make zero-shot predictions without manual feature engineering or task-specific retraining.
key_takeaways: Outperforms existing tabular foundation models on TabArena, TALENT, and BCC benchmarks.
Feature attention weights directly encode causal relationships.
Recovers causal skeletons zero-shot from structured datasets.
technical_architecture: Contextual Mechanism Network (CMN) architecture.
Context-Conditional Masked Modeling (CCMM) pre-training.
Structural Causal Model (SCM) synthetic data generator.
technical_details: Pretrained across diverse graph structures and functional mechanisms.
Jointly models features and labels for flexible downstream query tasks.
GitHub repository and weights publicly released.
events.potential_impact: Brings causal reasoning capabilities to AI database agents, enabling deeper automated analytics.
events.action: Follow the LimiX-2 GitHub repository and review its approach to causal graph inference from SQL tables.

events.title: Claude Code Ultimate Guide & Anthropic-Skills Ecosystem: Standardizing Harnesses and SKILL.md
events.tldr: A comprehensive community repository and open skill index showcase production engineering standards, SKILL.md formats, context boundary engineering, and harness designs for Claude Code.
events.what_happened: The community expanded the Claude Code Ultimate Guide repo alongside 125+ open SKILL.md packages under the `anthropic-skills` ecosystem, standardizing agent capabilities across IDEs.
events.what_changed: Agent development is shifting from ad-hoc prompting to strict harness engineering, context boundary isolation, and modular SKILL.md tool definitions.
events.why_it_matters: Provides a clean blueprint for building deterministic agent loops, managing context windows, and organizing tool libraries for coding and task agents.
key_takeaways: Harness engineering isolates deterministic workflow logic from stochastic LLM calls.
SKILL.md standard defines tool schemas, system context requirements, and execution constraints.
Modular skill repositories enable cross-editor agent compatibility (Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode).
technical_architecture: Agent harnesses enforce strict input/output boundaries around CLI tools and MCP servers.
SKILL.md metadata files declare dependencies, permissions, and step execution protocols.
technical_details: Guide repository contains 1,000+ commits spanning memory architectures, security sandboxing, and evaluation.
Topic index includes production tools for OOXML handling, code execution sandboxes, and legal/academic skills.
events.potential_impact: Accelerates the adoption of modular, interoperable agent skills across open-source and commercial agent frameworks.
events.action: Create a custom SKILL.md file for a local Python agent tool and integrate it into an agent harness loop.

events.title: Edge0: Serving 35B MoEs from SSD at 20 tok/s via Trained Pre-Router Prediction
events.tldr: Edge0 uses a one-step-ahead pre-router head and unmerged recovery LoRA to stream 35B MoE expert weights from SSD to GPU, keeping peak VRAM under 3 GB at 20 tokens/sec.
events.what_happened: Researchers introduced Edge0, an open-source streaming MoE inference engine that enables running a 35B Mixture-of-Experts model inside 3 GiB of active VRAM on a single 24GB GPU at 20 tokens per second.
events.what_changed: Previously, offloading MoE expert weights to SSD failed because layer N+1's routing could not be determined until layer N completed, forcing compute pipelines to stall while waiting for disk I/O.
events.why_it_matters: Edge0 solves this latency penalty with a per-layer pre-router head that predicts layer N+1's expert selection one token in advance. This allows weight prefetches to run concurrently with layer N compute while recovery LoRAs compensate for INT4 quantization and prediction noise.
key_takeaways: Pre-routing one token ahead completely hides SSD read latencies behind layer execution compute.
Recovery LoRA trained on the student path recovers quality lost to INT4 quantization and pre-routing replacements.
Allows developers to run 35B parameter MoEs on budget consumer GPUs without needing expensive multi-GPU setups.
technical_architecture: A per-layer pre-router head predicts routing indices for layer N+1 using layer N input states.
4-bit quantized expert weights are prefetched from NVMe SSD into a 3 GiB GPU sliding window buffer.
An unmerged recovery LoRA is executed during forward pass to restore FP16 teacher quality.
technical_details: Sustains 20 tok/s on a single 24GB consumer machine.
Maintains model output quality within a few benchmark points of FP16 non-quantized baselines.
Tested across 8B and 35B parameter MoE models with full open-source serving code in SGLang.
events.potential_impact: Dramatically lowers the hardware barrier for self-hosting high-parameter agent LLMs on affordable consumer gear.
events.action: Clone Edge0 from GitHub and benchmark a local 35B MoE model stream on a single GPU setup using 3 GB active VRAM.

events.title: Architectural Model Growth & Looping Alter Transformer Scaling Laws (20x Compute Efficiency)
events.tldr: Recursive depth and model growth in looped transformers modify pre-training scaling exponents, allowing a 7.4B model to match GPT-3 13B performance with 20x less compute.
events.what_happened: A research team demonstrated that architectural interventions like recursive looping and boundary operators fundamentally alter compute scaling exponents in LLM pre-training.
events.what_changed: Standard scaling laws assumed fixed compute-to-parameter ratios; this study proves that dynamic computational depth via layer looping dramatically increases compute efficiency at scale.
events.why_it_matters: For developers and model creators constrained by training budgets, increasing usable transformer depth dynamically yields exponential gains over traditional scaling.
key_takeaways: Looping (recursive depth) provides a dynamic growth mechanism by increasing loop passes during training.
A 7.4B looped model matches a standard GPT-3 13B model on CORE tasks using 20x less compute.
Boundary operators (normalizing and re-injecting earlier block outputs) enhance depth efficiency in vanilla transformers.
technical_architecture: Shared weight transformer blocks are looped dynamically based on compute budget.
Boundary operators normalize representations from early layers and re-inject them into deeper execution paths.
During data-constrained multi-epoch training, increasing loop count acts as an optimal regularizer.
technical_details: Evaluated across various model sizes and dataset compute budgets.
Demonstrated scaling exponent shifts that widen compute efficiency gaps as training scale increases.
events.potential_impact: Rethinks foundation model pre-training, making small, deeply recurrent models capable of competing with models twice their parameter size.
events.action: Read the paper's section on computational depth and test recursive layer looping in a small PyTorch transformer implementation.

events.title: Machine-Speed Security Architecture: Defense Strategies Against Autonomous AI Exploitation
events.tldr: AWS outlines continuous security defense architectures designed to withstand autonomous vulnerability scanners (e.g. Claude Mythos) and agent tool-chain exfiltration risks.
events.what_happened: AWS published an architectural guidance report on continuous automated defense, citing the impact of AI vulnerability discovery models (Claude Mythos Preview) and LLM-specific exfiltration threats.
events.what_changed: Security cycles are transitioning from weekly/quarterly manual red-teaming to real-time machine-speed detection, requiring zero-trust identity for autonomous agents.
events.why_it_matters: As agents gain execution permissions and tool access, prompt injection, tool misuse, and agent-chain exfiltration become primary attack vectors that require automated continuous safeguards.
key_takeaways: Autonomous AI tools can discover software vulnerabilities and generate working PoCs in hours.
Proper granular access control (CapBAC) prevented 97% of unauthorized AI access incidents.
Extensive AI security automation reduces incident lifecycles by 80 days and mitigates tool-hijacking risks.
technical_architecture: Continuous vulnerability scanning pipelines hooked directly into CI/CD build steps.
Out-of-band monitoring and access boundary enforcement for agent tool calling chains.
Zero-trust credential scoping per agent execution turn.
technical_details: Addresses OWASP Top 10 for LLMs including prompt injection and tool misuse.
Demonstrates automated patch deployment architectures to counter machine-speed exploits.
events.potential_impact: Forces agent engineers to implement automated access guards and runtime sandboxing as mandatory architecture components.
events.action: Implement strict input validation and access token scoping on all tool execution endpoints in your agent projects.

events.title: Fathom: Adaptive Per-Query Read Depth for Offloaded Long-Context KV Caches
events.tldr: Fathom stores 4-bit KV caches channel-major as bitplanes, allowing each query to dynamically adjust bit-read depth across offloaded host RAM to speed up million-token decode steps by 1.67x.
events.what_happened: Fathom introduced a per-query adaptive bit-depth scanning method for sparse decoding over host-RAM offloaded KV caches during ultra-long agent sessions.
events.what_changed: In 1M+ token agent sessions, host-RAM index scans bound decode speed. Existing methods (Double Sparsity, SparQ) read fixed 136-bit indices per token; Fathom dynamically allocates bit reads based on query variance.
events.why_it_matters: Long-horizon agent execution quickly exhausts GPU VRAM, forcing KV caches into host RAM. Fathom reduces PCIe/host-RAM bandwidth transfer by 18% while outperforming fixed-bit scans in accuracy.
key_takeaways: Channel-major bitplane storage turns prefix reads into native multi-bit quantizers.
Queries use reverse water-filling over channel variance to spend bit budgets optimally.
Achieves 1.67x faster GPU decode time on Qwen3-8B at 1,000,000 context tokens.
technical_architecture: The 4-bit K cache is stored channel-major as raw bitplanes in host RAM.
Reverse water-filling determines exact bit-plane read count per channel based on query importance.
Sparse top-k decoding fetches only selected winner rows into GPU SRAM.
technical_details: Matches exact top-k decoding accuracy on RULER benchmarks.
Reaches 136-bit scan step agreement on real coding-agent traces using only 92 bits.
events.potential_impact: Enables ultra-long agent sessions (1M+ tokens) to run at interactive speeds on offloaded host RAM architectures.
events.action: Monitor Fathom's open-source implementation for integration into vLLM and SGLang long-context serving backends.

events.title: CERA-MoA: Co-Evolving Router and LoRA Agents via Hidden-State Familiarity Estimation
events.tldr: CERA-MoA continuously co-evolves a dynamic router and independent LoRA agents using mid-layer hidden state familiarity estimators to route queries with minimal compute.
events.what_happened: Tsinghua University researchers released CERA-MoA, an iterative reinforcement learning framework where a routing mechanism and specialized sub-agents co-evolve simultaneously.
events.what_changed: Existing Mixture-of-Agents (MoA) architectures froze either the router or the sub-agents; CERA-MoA allows both to evolve dynamically using fast mid-layer hidden-state probes.
events.why_it_matters: Evaluates agent competence without running expensive full LLM rollouts, selecting only the smallest necessary subset of agents to solve a task efficiently.
key_takeaways: Predictive familiarity estimator uses mid-layer hidden states to assess agent competence instantly.
Cumulative-threshold routing dynamically activates minimal agent subsets per query.
Co-evolution with RL encourages strong specialization across individual LoRA sub-agents.
technical_architecture: Sub-agents are parameterized as lightweight domain LoRA adapters.
A router probes layer N hidden states of sub-agents to compute semantic familiarity scores.
Adaptive thresholding selects top-k sub-agents for downstream response generation.
technical_details: Outperforms static routing and fixed workflow fine-tuning baselines.
Open-source implementation available on GitHub.
events.potential_impact: Reduces multi-agent token overhead while improving specialized capabilities across complex multi-domain workflows.
events.action: Examine CERA-MoA's repository to understand how mid-layer representation probing can replace full agent dry-runs.

events.title: Andromeda 2: Autonomous Lab Optimization via Structured Evidence Grounding
events.tldr: Andromeda 2 combines structured internal evidence with autonomous tool invocation to design physical experiments, outperforming traditional Bayesian optimization by 3x.
events.what_happened: Researchers introduced Andromeda 2, an autonomous agent system that designs, invokes, and executes physical lab experiment batches by reasoning over structured historical data.
events.what_changed: Traditional Design-of-Experiments (DoE) and Bayesian optimization rely purely on statistical boundaries; Andromeda 2 grounds LLM tool calls in historical experimental evidence databases.
events.why_it_matters: Proves that combining RAG over structured experimental evidence with multi-step tool-calling loops dramatically outperforms classical mathematical optimization in complex physical search spaces.
key_takeaways: Achieved a 50% high-performance hit rate compared to 17% for probabilistic models and 2% for standard DoE.
Ablation studies confirmed that structured evidence grounding increased performance metrics by 34%.
Demonstrates real-world economic value for fully autonomous agent-driven experiment cycles.
technical_architecture: LLM planner queries a structured PostgreSQL/graph database of historical experimental trials.
Decision engine generates parameter payloads for automated laboratory hardware.
Feedback loop ingests new sensor readings to update the knowledge store continuously.
technical_details: Designed and evaluated on complex pharmaceutical SEDDS formulation tasks.
Identified 12 target-compliant formulations compared to 6 by previous state-of-the-art models.
events.potential_impact: Provides an architectural template for enterprise autonomous decision systems operating in lab, industrial, or complex business environments.
events.action: Build a mini feedback-loop agent that queries historical SQLite test runs before generating new test configuration parameters.

events.title: rMuscle: Dual-Phase Muscle Memory Caching Accelerates VLA Model Inference by 1.4x
events.tldr: rMuscle exploits repetitive action patterns in VLA agents using visual Context Caches and activation Action Caches, speeding up execution by up to 1.42x on RTX 4090 and Jetson Thor.
events.what_happened: Researchers created rMuscle, a real-time Vision-Language-Action (VLA) inference framework inspired by human muscle memory that caches repetitive internal states.
events.what_changed: Standard VLA inference recomputes full visual and action tokens on every timestep regardless of task repetition or static environment context.
events.why_it_matters: In repetitive robotic or agent loops, internal neural activations remain highly similar across steps; caching these patterns drastically reduces latency without sacrificing action accuracy.
key_takeaways: Context Cache reuses visual token representations across similar task trajectories.
Action Cache reuses neuron activation patterns across consecutive denoising steps.
Delivers 1.29x-1.42x speedup on consumer GPUs (RTX 4090) and edge devices (Jetson Thor).
technical_architecture: Dual-phase cache architecture operating across context processing and action generation.
Online sliding-window retrieval matches incoming states with cached token features.
Mask sharing across consecutive denoising steps minimizes weight memory accesses.
technical_details: Evaluated on LIBERO, RoboTwin, and physical robotic control benchmarks.
Zero drop in task success rate while achieving real-time latency gains.
events.potential_impact: Significantly improves the control loop frequency and responsiveness of VLA models deployed on edge hardware.
events.action: Study how activation caching patterns can be applied to textual agent loops with repetitive environment states.

events.title: Zing-0.5: Open-Source 5B Autoregressive World Model with Real-Time Joint Control
events.tldr: Zing-0.5 is an open-source 5B parameter autoregressive world model driving 24 FPS real-time interactive generation via unified action and text conditioning.
events.what_happened: Researchers introduced Zing-0.5, a 5B world model capable of generating real-time interactive 480p visual environments controlled simultaneously by keyboard input and streaming text instructions.
events.what_changed: Previous video generation models were static offline generators; Zing-0.5 enables continuous 24 FPS interactive streaming at under $0.01 per minute.
events.why_it_matters: Opens possibilities for building simulated training environments, game worlds, and visual feedback benchmarks for vision-based agents.
key_takeaways: Unifies magnitude-aware keyboard controls with temporally aligned text commands.
4-step distillation enables 24 FPS streaming at 832x480 resolution.
Weights, inference code, and SGLang serving backend fully open-sourced.
technical_architecture: Block-level causal student model distilled from segment-level teacher using distribution matching.
Context-preserving streaming context cache maintains long-horizon spatial consistency.
technical_details: Achieves 81.0 overall score on WBench Navigation benchmark.
Runs on consumer-grade server hosting at ~$0.009 per stream-minute.
events.potential_impact: Provides an accessible foundation for building interactive simulated environments for agent RL and visual world modeling.
events.action: Download the Zing-0.5 weights and run the interactive demo stream to test real-time action-conditioned generation.

events.title: ActionPiece: Physical Rank Consistency Tokenization for Autoregressive VLA Models
events.tldr: ActionPiece introduces Physical Rank Consistency (PRC) tokenization for VLA models, ensuring discrete action tokens preserve local physical distance rankings.
events.what_happened: ActionPiece was introduced as a new action tokenizer for autoregressive Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, replacing standard MSE-based pointwise reconstruction.
events.what_changed: Traditional action tokenizers evaluated quality via point error (MSE), causing similar spatial actions to collapse into single representation clusters and distorting fine control movements.
events.why_it_matters: High-fidelity spatial control requires action tokenizers to maintain relative physical ordering so subtle policy adjustments result in proportional hardware movements.
key_takeaways: Physical Rank Consistency (PRC) measures whether physical distance rankings are preserved after token quantization.
Joint supervision combines representation learning with physical distance order constraints.
Demonstrates significant performance gains on Qwen3-VL-4B policy setups.
technical_architecture: Encoder maps continuous action trajectories into discrete codeword distributions.
Physical rank preservation loss enforces near-far ordering in feature space.
A frozen decoder converts discrete tokens back into executable continuous commands.
technical_details: Tested on standard VLA control tasks with Qwen3-VL-4B policy backends.
Significantly outperforms standard VQ-VAE and BPE action tokenizers on precision tasks.
events.potential_impact: Sets a new standard for tokenizing continuous physical motor control variables in autoregressive multimodal architectures.
events.action: Study how Physical Rank Consistency loss functions differ from MSE in continuous-to-discrete tokenization.

events.title: GPT-Policy: In-Context Robot Learning via Frontier VLM Agents
events.tldr: GPT-Policy enables robots to adapt to new tasks zero-shot using VLM in-context learning and verified control loops without gradient updates.
events.what_happened: Researchers introduced GPT-Policy, a framework where VLM agents (such as GPT-6 Astra) interpret human video demonstrations and context to execute verifiable robotic manipulation actions in real time.
events.what_changed: Before, robotic adaptation required task-specific fine-tuning or parameter updates; now, VLMs learn new contact-sensitive behaviors purely in-context through execution feedback.
events.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that agentic scaffoldings combining context compilation and constrained verification controllers can achieve physical tool manipulation without retraining model weights.
key_takeaways: In-context learning enables zero-shot robot adaptation without gradient updates
Context compiler preserves task-relevant visual transitions for VLM decision-making
Constrained controller verifies and executes actions before sending outcome feedback
technical_architecture: Context Compiler filtering visual transitions into structured history
VLM Agent proposing high-level robot-tool action primitives
Constrained Execution Controller verifying safety constraints and reporting outcomes
technical_details: Evaluated on GPT-6 Astra VLM agent architecture
Zero gradient updates required during deployment adaptation
Closed-loop feedback via interaction outcomes
events.potential_impact: Accelerates deployment of generalist robotic agents in dynamic environments using standard LLM/VLM tool-calling patterns.
events.action: Study how the context compiler filters interaction history into structured observation-action-outcome tuples for zero-shot VLM agent controllers.

events.title: ComPO: Comparison-Based Zeroth-Order Preference Alignment for LLMs
events.tldr: ComPO introduces a zeroth-order comparison oracle alignment framework that outperforms direct preference optimization by mitigating likelihood displacement.
events.what_happened: Researchers proposed Comparison-based Preference Optimization (ComPO), extracting directional gradient signals from preference pairs without directly optimizing a differentiable loss function.
events.what_changed: Traditional DPO methods suffer from likelihood displacement on narrow margins; ComPO uses comparison mechanisms and unlabeled policy generations for reverse-KL control.
events.why_it_matters: Provides a robust mathematical alternative to DPO for aligning open-weight models (Llama, Gemma, Qwen) with higher length-controlled win rates.
key_takeaways: Zeroth-order comparison oracles prevent likelihood displacement on small likelihood margins
Online ComPO uses unlabeled policy generations to maintain reverse-KL control
Consistently improves length-controlled win rates across frontier open models
technical_architecture: Offline comparison oracle for non-differentiable preference extraction
Online reverse-KL regularization using unlabelled policy outputs
Constrained optimization scheme under local sample coverage
technical_details: Validated on Mistral, Llama, Gemma-2, Qwen3, Gemma-3
Proven theoretical convergence under gradient sparsity assumptions
39-page formal proof and pair-level diagnostic evaluation
events.potential_impact: Improves preference fine-tuning stability and performance for open-source foundation model custom alignments.
events.action: Track ComPO implementation code releases to evaluate as an alternative alignment method for custom fine-tuned assistant models.

events.title: Tokenizer Mechanics: Search Procedure Dominates Objective Function
events.tldr: EMNLP 2026 study proves bottom-up search (BPE) drives lower bits-per-byte in language models, regardless of optimization objective.
events.what_happened: Researchers introduced BottomUpLL and TopDownComp tokenizers to complete a 2x2 grid, isolating tokenizer search procedure from optimization objective.
events.what_changed: Previously, BPE and UnigramLM differences were conflated; researchers now prove search strategy (bottom-up vs top-down) drives compression efficiency, not the objective.
events.why_it_matters: Understanding tokenizer design aids in building custom domain-specific tokenizers for structured agent workflows, code generation, and multilingual data.
key_takeaways: Search procedure is the primary determinant of language model bits-per-byte efficiency
Bottom-up tokenizers consistently outperform top-down pruning methods in compression
Downstream syntactic tasks (BLiMP) show no strict sensitivity to tokenizer design
technical_architecture: 2x2 factorial evaluation matrix: Compression vs Likelihood / Bottom-Up vs Top-Down
BottomUpLL: Bottom-up likelihood-based greedy tokenization algorithm
TopDownComp: Top-down compression-based pruning tokenization algorithm
technical_details: Evaluated across English-only and multilingual datasets
Accepted at EMNLP 2026
Evaluated on bits-per-byte and BLiMP benchmarks
events.potential_impact: Guides more principled construction of custom tokenizers for specialized code and multilingual language models.
events.action: Review the BottomUpLL implementation to understand how bottom-up vocabulary selection impacts LLM context window efficiency.

events.title: PANORAMA: Panoptic Grounded Captioning via Proposal Selection
events.tldr: PANORAMA links VLM textual phrase generation directly to pixel-level segment masks via phrase-conditioned proposal selection.
events.what_happened: Researchers created PanoCaps and PANORAMA, a VLM framework conditioning pretrained segmenters on textual phrase representations to select precise entity-level masks.
events.what_changed: Prior grounded VLMs produced either incomplete descriptions or inaccurate masks; PANORAMA unifies detailed text generation with precise multi-instance pixel segmentation.
events.why_it_matters: Enables visual GUI and computer-use agents to ground text referring expressions directly to exact pixel boundaries and UI element masks.
key_takeaways: Conditions segmenters directly on phrase representations for joint captioning and mask selection
Generalized Panoptic Quality (gPQ) metric evaluates textual and mask consistency jointly
Supports single-region and multi-instance referring phrase grounding
technical_architecture: Phrase-conditioned mask proposal pool generated from pretrained segmenter
VLM selection head mapping textual referring expressions to candidate masks
Joint loss optimization balancing caption fluency and segmentation accuracy
technical_details: PanoCaps benchmark with human-annotated entity-level alignment
Supports both foreground objects and background region segmentation
Code and dataset publicly released
events.potential_impact: Improves visual grounding accuracy for autonomous computer-use agents operating on complex graphical interfaces.
events.action: Test PANORAMA open-source code to evaluate phrase-to-mask mapping performance on web browser and UI element detection tasks.

events.title: Audio-Visual Force Profiling for Closed-Loop Manipulation Agents
events.tldr: Researchers use generated contact sound loudness to derive time-varying force profiles for zero-shot robotic force regulation.
events.what_happened: A novel pipeline combines video and audio generation models to extract kinematic trajectories and desired contact force profiles from natural language prompts.
events.what_changed: Generative video baselines produce purely kinematic trajectories lacking force; this framework uses generated contact sound intensity to shape dynamic force profiles.
events.why_it_matters: Shows how multimodal generative models can create rich physical world feedback representations for closed-loop execution controllers without physical force sensors.
key_takeaways: Generated contact audio loudness maps directly to desired physical force profiles
Closed-loop force regulators track sound-shaped profiles during task execution
Serves as an automated synthetic data generation engine for physical policy training
technical_architecture: Text-to-Video and Text-to-Audio generative models driven by task prompts
Sound loudness envelope extractor converting decibels to target contact forces
Closed-loop force regulator on Franka Panda tracking trajectory and target force
technical_details: Tested zero-shot on physical Franka Panda robot arm
Outperforms kinematic-only video trajectory generation baselines
Synthetic data generation engine for contact-rich tasks
events.potential_impact: Enables low-cost multimodal simulation of tactile and force feedback for physical agent policy training.
events.action: Examine how multimodal generation can synthesize non-visual feedback channels (e.g. audio loudness) into numeric control parameters.

events.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Consent Portal: Per-User OAuth Session Binding for MCP Clients
events.tldr: AWS released a managed Consent portal in Bedrock AgentCore to securely manage and bind per-user OAuth tokens for MCP tool calls.
events.what_happened: AWS introduced a managed Consent portal for AgentCore Gateway, resolving user identity binding and token storage when AI agents invoke external services.
events.what_changed: Before, developers had to build custom callback servers for OAuth session binding. Now, AgentCore handles browser redirects and stores tokens in a vault.
events.why_it_matters: Enables multi-user MCP clients like Claude Code, Cursor, and VS Code to safely execute user-authenticated API tools without token leakage.
key_takeaways: Binds identity provider OAuth grants directly to individual agent execution sessions
Tokens are securely persisted in AgentCore Identity vault for repeated tool calls
Compatible with MCP clients including Claude Code, Cursor, and Visual Studio Code
technical_architecture: AgentCore Gateway session binding endpoint with corporate IdP integration
Encrypted AgentCore Identity token vault for storing per-user OAuth tokens
AWS CloudTrail audit logging for every authenticated agent tool invocation
technical_details: OAuth 2.0 authorization code grant flow with session binding
CompleteResourceTokenAuth API integration for token exchange
Pre-invocation consent verification in MCP tool execution loops
events.potential_impact: Eliminates custom authentication harnesses for enterprise MCP servers, reducing identity security risks in production multi-tenant agent deployments.
events.action: Implement AgentCore Identity Consent portal flows when building multi-user MCP servers requiring user-scoped API permissions.

events.title: TypeSafe Jev: RLCD-Trained Non-Autoregressive System One Model for Sub-Millisecond Agent Routing
events.tldr: TypeSafe released Jev, a non-autoregressive decision model trained via RLCD that routes agent tool calls over 100x faster than small LLMs.
events.what_happened: TypeSafe launched Jev, a specialized non-generative model designed strictly for classification, scoring, and tool routing without autoregressive string generation.
events.what_changed: Before, agent loops relied on expensive, slow LLMs for routing. Now, Jev executes deterministic routing decisions with parallel sampling and zero hallucination.
events.why_it_matters: Drastically slashes agent loop latency and token costs by offloading control flow, gating, and tool selection away from slow reasoning models.
key_takeaways: Delivers 20x to 200x faster execution than small frontier LLMs
Operates 40x to 400x cheaper than standard autoregressive models
Trained via Reinforcement Learning from Calibrated Decisions (RLCD)
technical_architecture: Non-autoregressive classifier architecture for parallel logit decision sampling
Calibrated logit scoring system eliminating generative hallucination risk
System One complementary layer positioned in front of System Two LLMs
technical_details: RLCD optimization for calibrated confidence scores across discrete actions
Sub-millisecond inference execution for agent loop conditional branching
Structured input parsing for direct routing array outputs

events.title: RetireOPD & EOS Alignment Fix Length Inflation in Agent Reinforcement Learning
events.tldr: RetireOPD and EOS token alignment solve length inflation and sparse reward limits in multi-turn RL agents, yielding substantial benchmark gains.
events.what_happened: Two research papers introduced RetireOPD (adaptive teacher retirement in on-policy distillation) and EOS semantic alignment to stabilize multi-turn agent RL.
events.what_changed: Before, on-policy distillation suffered from termination mismatch and fixed schedules. Now, dynamic retirement and shared EOS actions stabilize student generation length.
events.why_it_matters: Provides practical algorithms for training small open-weight models into highly efficient multi-turn web and environment control agents.
key_takeaways: Adaptive retirement drops teacher supervision once student-teacher discrepancy stops shrinking
Unifies functional EOS tokens across student and teacher vocabularies
Surpasses skill-conditioned teacher performance on ALFWorld and WebShop
technical_architecture: Decoupled skill-conditioned teacher paired with skill-free student model
Adaptive Retirement mechanism monitoring performance gap during RL
Shared semantic stopping action for mismatched EOS token sets
technical_details: +14.1% to +18.8% ALFWorld success rate gain on Qwen2.5
+11.8% to +19.0% WebShop accuracy gain
Eliminates generation budget exhaustion in Qwen3 and Llama OPD runs
events.potential_impact: Accelerates training of small, highly reliable agent models on multi-turn web navigation and task completion tasks.
events.action: Study the RetireOPD paper to learn how adaptive teacher retirement prevents student over-fitting in trajectory distillation.
verified_facts: RetireOPD improves ALFWorld success rate by 14.1% to 18.8% over RL baselines across Qwen2.5 models
Improves WebShop accuracy by 11.8% to 19.0% and surpasses its own skill-conditioned teacher model
Identified termination token mismatch between student and teacher as key driver of generation budget exhaustion
Treating functionally equivalent EOS tokens as shared semantic stop action mitigates length inflation
events.interpretation: Adaptive retirement and semantic termination alignment prevent RL agents from over-generating tokens during multi-turn task runs.
events.uncertainty: Optimal student-teacher retirement thresholds vary depending on task trajectory depth.
events.counter_argument: Fixed length-penalty reward functions can sometimes curb inflation without joint teacher training overhead.

events.title: Google Agent Substrate: ღია კოდის მაღალი სიმკვრივის გაშვების გარემო AI აგენტებისთვის GKE-ზე
events.tldr: Google-მა გამოუშვა Agent Substrate GKE-ზე, რაც აგენტებს აძლევს 10x უფრო მკვრივ, sub-500ms suspend/resume უსაფრთხო იზოლირებულ runtime-ს.

events.what_changed: მძიმე კონტეინერული VM-ების ნაცვლად მივიღეთ ნულოვანი ნდობის kernel იზოლაცია და მყისიერი suspend/resume უმოქმედო აგენტებისთვის.
events.why_it_matters: შენს coding agent პროექტებში საშუალებას მოგცემს უსაფრთხოდ გაუშვა LLM-ის გენერირებული bash ბრძანებები და კოდი მინიმალური latency-ით.
key_takeaways: 10x მაღალი density კონტეინერებთან შედარებით

verified_facts: Agent Substrate უზრუნველყოფს 10x მაღალ density-ს სტანდარტულ კონტეინერებთან შედარებით

Nous Research-ის Hermes Agent უკვე აგებულია Agent Substrate-ის ბაზაზე GKE-ზე
events.interpretation: ავტონომიური აგენტების ინფრასტრუქტურა შორდება მძიმე VM-ებს და გადადის მიკრო-სენდბოქსებზე, სადაც უმოქმედო აგენტის state მომენტალურად იყინება resouces-ის დასაზოგად.
events.uncertainty: უცნობია Agent Substrate-ის self-hosted დაყენების სირთულე vanilla Kubernetes კლასტერებზე GKE-ს ფარგლებს გარეთ.

events.title: Google Mantis: Pre-Submit მრავალ-აგენტიანი უსაფრთხოების ჰარნესი კოდის ლოკალური მუქარის მოდელებით

events.what_happened: Google-ის ინფრასტრუქტურულმა გუნდმა გააზიარა არქიტექტურა, რომელიც AI აგენტებს იყენებს ყოველი commit-ის უსაფრთხოების შესამოწმებლად რეალურ დროში.
events.what_changed: იშვიათი და ნელი დიდი სკანირებების ნაცვლად, კონტექსტური აგენტები ამოწმებენ ცალკეულ diff-ებს პირდაპირ დეველოპერის workflow-ში.
events.why_it_matters: გაჩვენებს, თუ როგორ შეიძლება ააგო CI/CD bot ან GitHub Action აგენტი, რომელიც მხოლოდ ზედაპირულ linting-ს კი არა, ღრმა არქიტექტურულ უსაფრთხოებას ამოწმებს.
key_takeaways: Pre-submit სკანირება commit-ის ეტაპზე
False-positive მაჩვენებლის ვარდნა 3%-მდე
Dependency call graph-ების ინტეგრაცია კონტექსტისთვის

Live codebase metadata threat modeling
Cross-package dependency call graph traversal
technical_details: Real-time pre-submit evaluation

AST and dependency graph context feeding

verified_facts: Google-ის Mantis სისტემა ახორციელებს უწყვეტ pre-submit სკანირებას ასობით მილიონ კოდის ხაზზე

სისტემა ყოველთვიურად ასობით დაუცველობის შეღწევას აჩერებს production ინფრასტრუქტურაში
events.interpretation: კოდის გენერაციის ზრდასთან ერთად, უსაფრთხოების შემოწმება გადადის static analysis-იდან მრავალ-აგენტიან contextual review-ზე უშუალოდ git pre-submit ეტაპზე.
events.uncertainty: Mantis-ის სრული ინტეგრაცია მოითხოვს მთლიანი კოდის ბაზის dependency call graph-ის რეალურ დროში განახლებას.
events.counter_argument: Pre-commit ან pre-submit ეტაპზე LLM აგენტების გაშვებამ შესაძლოა გაზარდოს PR შემოწმების დრო და შეაფერხოს დეველოპერთა მუშაობა.

events.title: When2Think: სირთულეზე მორგებული გამოთვლის განაწილება ჰიბრიდული მსჯელობის მოდელებისთვის
events.tldr: When2Think პოსტ-ტრენინგით ასწავლის მოდელს, როდის უპასუხოს მომენტალურად (System 1) და როდის დახარჯოს reasoning ტოკენები (System 2).
events.what_happened: Microsoft-ის მკვლევრებმა წარადგინეს ჩარჩო, რომელიც არეგულირებს მსჯელობის სიგრძეს ამოცანის სირთულის მიხედვით, learned reward model-ების გარეშე.
events.what_changed: ფიქსირებული length penalty-ს ნაცვლად, მოდელი მარტივ ამოცანებს ხსნის პირდაპირ, ხოლო რთულ პრობლემებზე რთავს გაფართოებულ CoT ჯაჭვს.
events.why_it_matters: დაგეხმარება გაიგო reasoning მოდელების token ეკონომიკა და შეიმუშაო prompt routing სტრატეგიები აგენტების გამოძახებების გასაიაფებლად.
key_takeaways: IDAC ჯილდოს ფორმირება რეფერენს სტატისტიკით
27.9%-იანი ტოკენების ეკონომია AIME 24-ზე
Critic-free ოპტიმიზაცია ონლაინ რეფერენს მოდელის გარეშე
technical_architecture: Instance-adaptive compute allocation
Verifier-based reward shaping
Batch-wise standardized advantages
technical_details: IDAC reward formulation
System 1 vs System 2 dynamic shift
Pass@3 metrics on AIME 24/25
events.potential_impact: შემცირდება საწარმოო API ხარჯები frontier reasoning მოდელების გამოყენებისას batch ამოცანების შესრულების დროს.
events.action: გააანალიზე შენი აგენტის პრომპტები და შექმენი lightweight კლასიფიკატორი, რომელიც მარტივ მოთხოვნებს უგზავნის Flash მოდელს, ხოლო რთულს Reasoning მოდელს.
verified_facts: When2Think იყენებს IDAC (Instance-level Difficulty-Aware Control) მექანიზმს reasoning სიღრმის სამართავად
AIME 24-ზე Pass@3 გაიზარდა 10.0%-ით, ხოლო token usage შემცირდა 27.9%-ით საბაზისო მოდელთან შედარებით
AIME 25-ზე მოდელმა მიაღწია 40.0% Pass@3 შედეგს და გადააჭარბა მარტივ routing ბაზისებს
events.interpretation: Reasoning მოდელები (o1/o3 სტილის) ხშირად ზედმეტად ფიქრობენ მარტივ ამოცანებზე; IDAC აბალანსებს System 1 (სწრაფი) და System 2 (ღრმა) რეჟიმებს token-ების დაზოგვით.
events.uncertainty: უცნობია რამდენად კარგად გადადის ეს მიდგომა მათემატიკური ამოცანებიდან პროგრამულ ინჟინერიასა და ზოგად agentic workflow-ებზე.
events.counter_argument: სირთულის არასწორმა შეფასებამ შესაძლოა გამოიწვიოს რთული ამოცანების ნაადრევი direct answering და შეცდომების ზრდა.

events.title: Score Centering: Off-Policy RL-ის სტაბილიზაცია Training-Inference შეუსაბამობისას LLM-ებში
events.tldr: Score Centering ამატებს მარტივ კორექციულ წევრს, რომელიც აბათილებს drift-ს და ასტაბილურებს LLM-ების RL წვრთნას სწრაფი rollout ძრავების გამოყენებისას.
events.what_happened: მკვლევრებმა აღმოაჩინეს, რომ off-policy reinforcement learning-ის დესტაბილიზაციას იწვევს მუდმივი bias წვრთნისა და rollout ძრავებს შორის, და შექმნეს ადიტიური კორექცია.
events.what_changed: ძვირადღირებული importance sampling-ის ან ინფერენსის სიჩქარის გაწირვის ნაცვლად, score centering ანულირებს დრიფტს მინიმალური გამოთვლითი დანახარჯით.
events.why_it_matters: კრიტიკულია, თუ მომავალში დააპირებ საკუთარი მცირე მოდელების post-training-ს ან local GRPO/PPO ექსპერიმენტებს სამუშაო სადგურზე.
key_takeaways: TIM არასტაბილურობის მთავარი მიზეზია სისტემური drift
Score centering მუშაობს 0.6B-30B მოდელებზე
თავსებადია importance sampling ალგორითმებთან
technical_architecture: Additive drift-canceling correction term
Engine mismatch compensation pipeline
Quantized inference rollout stabilization
technical_details: 0.6B to 30B parameter evaluation
TIM bias cancellation formula
Staleness experiment compatibility
events.potential_impact: საშუალებას აძლევს ინჟინრებს გამოიყენონ 4-bit ან 8-bit კვანტიზებული ინფერენს ძრავები მონაცემთა გენერაციისთვის RL წვრთნისას სტაბილურობის დაკარგვის გარეშე.
events.action: შეისწავლე training-inference mismatch-ის კონცეფცია LLM-ების reinforcement learning-ში და გაეცანი PPO/GRPO განახლების ფორმულებს.
verified_facts: კვლევამ აჩვენა, რომ TIM-ის (Training-Inference Mismatch) ქვეშ არასტაბილურობას იწვევს ძრავებს შორის დაგროვებადი დრიფტი
შემოთავაზებული დანამატი score centering წევრი აბათილებს დრიფტს და ასტაბილურებს RL-ს
მეთოდი გამოცდილია 0.6B-დან 30B პარამეტრიან მოდელებზე კვანტიზაციისა და staleness-ის პირობებში
events.interpretation: RL fine-tuning-ის დროს rollout ინფერენსისთვის ხშირად იყენებენ vLLM/TensorRT-ს კვანტიზაციით, რაც ქმნის სისტემურ ცდომილებას წვრთნის დროს; score centering ამ პრობლემას მარტივად აგვარებს.
events.uncertainty: არ არის ნაჩვენები მეთოდის ეფექტი 70B+ პარამეტრის მქონე frontier მოდელების სრულმასშტაბიან PPO/GRPO გაშვებებზე.
events.counter_argument: ინფერენსისა და წვრთნის ძრავების იდენტურ FP16/BF16 სიზუსტეზე შენარჩუნება სრულად გამორიცხავს TIM-ს, თუ compute ბიუჯეტი იძლევა ამის საშუალებას.

events.title: CliffCompaction: უდანაკარგო context compaction ხანგრძლივი coding აგენტებისთვის
events.tldr: CliffCompaction გთავაზობთ autocompaction ტექნიკას, რომელიც ინარჩუნებს ორიგინალ ტექსტს rewriting-ის გარეშე და ამცირებს ხარჯს 50%-ით.
events.what_happened: შექმნეს open-source API-proxy implementations CliffCompaction-ისთვის, რომელიც არასდროს აკეთებს კომპაქტირებული კონტექსტის განმეორებით კომპაქციას.
events.what_changed: LLM-generated summary-ების ნაცვლად გამოიყენება პირდაპირი truncation, რაც კვეთს context drift-ს 1-მილიონიან context window-ზე.
events.why_it_matters: Claude Code და Codex harness-ებთან ინტეგრაციით შეგიძლიათ მნიშვნელოვნად შეამციროთ API ხარჯები ხანგრძლივი დებSimpleDateFormat სესიებისას.
key_takeaways: ნულის ტოლფასი context drift ორიგინალი ტექსტის შენარჩუნებით
50%-მდე დაზოგილი ტოკენები bounded context window-ში
Scaffold-agnostic API-proxy ხელმისაწვდომია ღია კოდით
technical_architecture: API-proxy შრე harness-სა და LLM-ს შორის
Discard mechanics ძველი კომპაქტირებული ბუფერებისთვის
Zero-rephrase truncation ალგორითმი
technical_details: KernelBench 3.58x speedup 400 step-ზე
10+ პროცენტული პუნქტი Terminal-Bench-ზე
Claude Code და Codex-ის მხარდაჭერა
events.potential_impact: შემცირდება ხანგრძლივი აგენტური სესიების ფინანსური დანახარჯი და გაიზარდება კოდის გენერაციის სიზუსტე.
events.action: გამოცადეთ CliffCompaction-ის API-proxy მიდგომა თქვენს Python LLM wrapper-ში და შეადარეთ ტოკენების დანახარჯი პირდაპირ Prompt-ს.
verified_facts: CliffCompaction ამცირებს Token cost-ს 50%-მდე Terminal-Bench-ზე მუშაობისას
მეთოდი არასდროს აკეთებს ტექსტის rephrasing-ს ან rewriting-ს, მხოლოდ Truncation/Dropping-ს იყენებს
KernelBench-ზე 400 ნაბიჯის შემდეგ CUDA kernel speedup-მა მიაღწია 3.58x-ს
events.interpretation: LLM-ით კონტექსტის შეჯამება (summarization) იწვევს ინფორმაციის დამახინჯებას (context drift), რასაც აგვარებს მხოლოდ ზუსტი წაშლა/ამოჭრა.
events.uncertainty: არახელსაყრელ პირობებში Truncation-მა შესაძლოა წაშალოს იშვიათი, მაგრამ კრიტიკული დამოკიდებულებები კოდში.
events.counter_argument: სემანტიკური summarization ზოგჯერ აუცილებელია, როდესაც კოდის ფრაგმენტები ძალიან დიდი ზომისაა და უბრალო წაშლა აფუჭებს სინტაქსს.

events.title: A2M: სემანტიკური supply-chain შეტევები და აგენტის ჰაიჯექინგი MCP ეკოსისტემაში
events.tldr: A2M ჩარჩო აჩვენებს, თუ როგორ შეიძლება MCP აგენტის გადამისამართება და მონაცემთა გაჟონვა ინსტრუმენტის მეტამონაცემების მანიპულაციით.
events.what_happened: მკვლევარებმა შექმნეს A2M შეტევის მოდელი, რომელიც ორიენტირებულია MCP Tool-ების აღწერილობების ოპტიმიზაციაზე აგენტის მოტყუების მიზნით.
events.what_changed: ტრადიციული API endpoint მოწყვლადობებიდან ყურადღება გადავიდა LLM-ის სემანტიკური ძიების (semantic matching) სუსტ ადგილებზე.
events.why_it_matters: თუ აშენებთ MCP Server-ებს ან იყენებთ მესამე მხარის Tool-ებს, აუცილებელია შეამოწმოთ ინსტრუმენტების სემანტიკური ვალიდაცია.
key_takeaways: Attraction phase ზრდის მავნე tool-ის არჩევის შანსს
Manipulation phase ცვლის execution trace-ებს
74.4% success rate ინფორმაციის ექსფილტრაციაზე
technical_architecture: Two-stage black-box attack framework
Attraction metadata optimization module
Trace-optimized response manipulation
technical_details: 93.6% malicious tool invocation rate
32.4x token cost increase under DoS
LiveMCPBench-ზე ჩატარებული ტესტები
events.potential_impact: აუცილებელი გახდება runtime isolation და tool metadata-ს ხელით/მკაცრი სქემით დამოწმება MCP არქიტექტურებში.
events.action: შეისწავლეთ თქვენი MCP Server-ების schema validation და დაამატეთ strict regex / type assertions ინსტრუმენტის აღწერილობებს.
verified_facts: A2M იყენებს Attraction და Manipulation ეტაპებს MCP ინსტრუმენტების საიტაცებლად
GLM-4.6-ზე მავნე tool-ის გამოძახების სიხშირემ მიაღწია 93.6%-ს LiveMCPBench-ზე
Cognitive DoS შეტევით ტოკენების დანახარჯი გაიზარდა 32.4x-ით
events.interpretation: MCP-ის სემანტიკური tool selection მექანიზმი მოწყვლადია metadata poisoning-ის მიმართ, რაც მოითხოვს მკაცრ static validation შრეს.
events.uncertainty: უცნობია რამდენად ეფექტურად დაიცავს აგენტს ახალი intent-gating და Zero-Trust პროტოკოლები რეალურ production გარემოში.
events.counter_argument: მოდელების შემდგომმა alignment-მა შესაძლოა შეამციროს მავნე metadata-ს მიმართ მგრძნობელობა დამატებითი კოდის გარეშე.

events.title: Agensh: დეცენტრალიზებული მრავალ-აგენტიანი არქიტექტურის მასშტაბირება 1,024 აგენტამდე
events.tldr: Agensh წარმოადგენს უცენტრალო multi-agent harness-ს, რომელიც ასინქრონულად მასშტაბირდება 1,024 აგენტამდე 55%-იანი test-pass მაჩვენებლით.
events.what_happened: მკვლევარებმა წარადგინეს Agensh, სადაც აგენტები თვითონ იღებენ და ამოწმებენ დავალებებს shared workspace-ის მეშვეობით ცენტრალური კოორდინატორის გარეშე.
events.what_changed: ცენტრალიზებული router-ზე დაფუძნებული არქიტექტურა ჩანაცვლდა ასინქრონული self-organized loop-ით shared context-ის გარშემო.
events.why_it_matters: რთული coding project-ების გადასაჭრელად შეგიძლიათ გამოიყენოთ ბევრი მცირე აგენტი პარალელურად, ნაცვლად ერთი მონოლითური Prompt-ისა.
key_takeaways: ცენტრალური orchestrator-ის არარსებობა ხსნის სკალირების ბარიერს
Shared workspace მოიცავს proposed, ongoing და completed დავალებებს
1,024 აგენტზე pass rate გაიზარდა 21.17 პროცენტული პუნქტით
technical_architecture: Shared workspace ინახავს დავალებების სტატუსებს
Message interface უზრუნველყოფს ასინქრონულ კომუნიკაციას
Shared context ინარჩუნებს მიღწეულ შედეგებს

events.title: Growing Harness: აგენტის მართვის ლოგიკის გადატანა Context-იდან reusable კოდში
events.tldr: Growing Harness გარდაქმნის განმეორებად აგენტურ გადაწყვეტილებებს იაფ Code Harness-ად, რაც 90%-ით ამცირებს LLM გამოძახებებს.

events.what_changed: დაიმსხვრა მითი, რომ Type-Safe (JSON Schema / Enum) გამონატანი ავტომატურად ნიშნავს ლოგიკურად სწორ პასუხს.

verified_facts: 0/1 ოპციების სახელების no/yes-ით ჩანაცვლებამ შეცვალა 70.4 პასუხი 100-დან და AUC 0.94-დან 0.23-მდე დააგდო
Type-error rate რჩება 0%-ზე, მაშინაც კი, როდესაც გადაწყვეტილების სიზუსტე კატასტროფულად ეცემა
ნეიტრალური ან შემთხვევითი სტრიქონების (random strings) გამოყენება ოპციის სახელებად აბრუნებს მოდელს სტაბილურ რეჟიმში
events.interpretation: Typed/Structured Output-ები იძლევიან გარანტიას მხოლოდ სინტაქსზე და არა სემანტიკურ სიზუსტეზე; სემანტიკურად დატვირთული ოპციის სახელები აფუჭებენ რუბრიკის აღქმას.

events.title: The Tasteful Agent: ხანგრძლივ დავალებებში აგენტის გადაწყვეტილებების ხარისხის გაუმჯობესება
events.tldr: Microsoft-ის მკვლევარებმა შექმნეს Taste-Bench აგენტების გადაწყვეტილების ხარისხის გასაზომად და აჩვენეს, რომ Taste-ის სწავლება შესაძლებელია.
events.what_happened: წარმოადგინეს Taste-Bench, სადაც იზომება აგენტის Taste - უნარი აირჩიოს სწორი გზა Decision Fork-ის დროს.
events.what_changed: End-to-end წარმატების გაზომვის ნაცვლად, შეფასება ხდება უშუალოდ გადაწყვეტილების მიღების წერტილებში (forks).
events.why_it_matters: გეხმარებათ გაიგოთ, თუ რატომ იჭრებიან აგენტები ხანგრძლივ ამოცანებში და როგორ დაატრენინგოთ სტუდენტი მოდელები teacher feedback-ით.
key_takeaways: Top მოდელების სიზუსტე მხოლოდ 59.7%-ია

technical_architecture: Decision fork mining algorithm trajectories-დან
Teacher-student distillation architecture
No-lookahead fork evaluation module
technical_details: 59.7% top model accuracy on Taste-Bench

Distillation of outcome-aware teacher
events.potential_impact: შექმნის ახალ სტანდარტს აგენტების შიდა მსჯელობისა და გადაწყვეტილების მიღების ხარისხის შეფასებაში.
events.action: გაანალიზეთ თქვენი აგენტის სესიების Execution Traces და იპოვეთ Decision Fork-ები, სადაც არასწორი ინსტრუმენტი იქნა არჩეული.
verified_facts: Taste-Bench ზომავს აგენტის უნარს მიიღოს სწორი გადაწყვეტილება decision fork-ზე მომავალი შედეგის დაუნახავად
საუკეთესო ფრონტიერ მოდელმა Taste-Bench-ზე მიაღწია მხოლოდ 59.7%-იან სიზუსტეს
დიდი reasoning budget (CoT) არ აუმჯობესებს აგენტის Taste-ს გადაწყვეტილების მიღებისას
events.interpretation: აგენტების მთავარი პრობლემა არის არასწორი ჰიპოთეზის არჩევა საწყის ეტაპზე, რისი გამოსწორებაც დისტილაციით (distillation) არის შესაძლებელი.
events.uncertainty: ავტომატურად mined decision fork-ები შესაძლოა შეიცავდნენ ხმაურს და არ ასახავდნენ რეალურ ადამიანურ Taste-ს.
events.counter_argument: დამატებითი RL-ს ან მონტე-კარლოს ხის ძიების (MCTS) გამოყენებამ შესაძლოა გადაფაროს Taste-ის დეფეციტი ინფერენსის დროს.
